newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tentative German DAX supported by bank stocks.
newsitem.headline: Tentative German DAX supported by bank stocks.

text.p: Firm interest in blue chip banking stocks helped support the otherwise uneasy German share market on Monday, with the 30-share DAX index ending its rangebound bourse session just slightly weaker.
The DAX closed floor trade down 3.71 points at 2,994.53, but was up some 12 points from its late post-bourse close on Friday, despite a pre-weekend slide on Wall Street.

Dealers said the market was tense ahead of Wall Street's opening and key U.S. employment cost data due on Tuesday, and had not shown a clear trend. A report showing West German January CPI was 1.8 percent year-on-year had no impact.

"Things will get going properly tomorrow," said a Munich dealer. "The U.S. numbers will give us a whole new picture of what stocks are up against in terms of (interest) rate prospects and it should be a better day for home news as well."
Bank shares led advancers from the start ahead of dividend announcements expected from tomorrow from the biggest players.
Deutsche Bank, the heaviest-traded of the blue chip stocks, rose 80 pfennigs to 85.15 marks.

Deutsche's supervisory board meets tomorrow, an event usually followed by a dividend announcement, and Commerzbank, which rose 25 pfennigs to 43.80 marks, is to reveal its 1996 dividend in the morning.
Steelmaker Thyssen AG was up two marks at 292.50 marks, after the company issued full 1995/1996 results and said the overall outlook was positive.

Some dealers were still looking for a further correction on the DAX, which has surged dramatically in the past weeks, with one noting that it was almost impossible to attract investors with the blue chip index over 3,000 points.
"We need to get back to a lower base and then we can start the uptrend all over again," he said.
